name: Havasania
title: The Ancestor of the Rechabites
summary: Havasania (also known as Rekab or associated with the lineage of the Rechabites) was the ancestor of the Rechabites, a group known for their strict obedience to ancestral commands. The prophet Jeremiah used the Rechabites' faithfulness to Havasania's commands as an example and a contrast to Judah's disobedience toward God.

keyEvents.title: The Rechabite Rules for Living
keyEvents.description: Havasania (through his descendant Jonadab, son of Rekab) gave strict commands to his descendants not to drink wine, not to build houses, not to sow grain, and not to plant vineyards, but to live in tents all their lives.

keyEvents.title: The Rechabites Tested by Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: The prophet Jeremiah was instructed by God to invite the Rechabites into the temple and offer them wine to test their faithfulness to ancestral commands.

keyEvents.title: The Faithful Obedience of the Rechabites
keyEvents.description: The Rechabites refused to drink wine, explaining that they held fast to the commands of Jonadab, son of Rekab (of Havasania's lineage), which had been passed down to them.

keyEvents.title: God's Judgment on Judah in Contrast
keyEvents.description: God used the Rechabites' obedience to their ancestors' commands as a sharp contrast to Judah's disobedience to the Lord's own words and the warnings of the prophets.

keyEvents.title: God's Blessing on the Rechabites
keyEvents.description: Because of the Rechabites' faithfulness to the commands of Jonadab son of Recab, God promised that there would never lack a man from Jonadab's line to stand before him.
